data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The claim that a trained non-expert panel plus checklist beats a single expert is underdetermined within a single evaluation unless that evaluation is explicitly adversarial: genuine reliability manifests as robustness to distribution shift, which cannot be tested on in-distribution items, so the evidence must be constructed by including items where the checklist's surface features are designed to mislead.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the evaluation cannot ethically or practically include adversarial items (e.g., real medical diagnosis), this evidence is uncollectable.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the expert also fails the adversarial items, the panel's success, while evidence of genuine reliability, does not prove it beats the expert.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the checklist is robust to all practical adversarial perturbations, the gap is zero even if the panel is merely compliant.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Reliability is not accuracy on average; it is accuracy under perturbation. A single evaluation on standard items measures accuracy, not reliability. To measure reliability, the evaluation must include perturbed items (e.g., cases where a checklist step is a distractor). On standard items, compliance and competence are confounded. On adversarial items, they diverge: the compliant panel follows the distractor and fails; the competent panel overrides and succeeds. Thus, the evidence is the performance gap on adversarial items within the evaluation.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
